observations:
Torah LM2/25 contains no bechina language in the source text — no explicit statements of the form 'X הוא בחינת Y' or 'X נקרא Y' that would establish conceptual equivalences between three or more independent concepts forming a new domain.

The spec for new packages requires: '3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language in the source text that form an independent domain not covered by the existing packages.' This criterion is not met.

Candidate clusters examined:

1. HITBODEDUT / SICHA / TEFILA cluster: These three concepts (solitary practice, personal speech, prayer) are closely related in the text and could intuitively form a package. However, the Rebbe never says 'hitbodedut IS sicha' or 'sicha IS tefila' using bechina language. He says: 'וּתְפִלָּה וְשִׂיחָה זוֹ' — treating them as the same activity by description, but the statement is descriptive/definitional ('this prayer and this speech'), not an ontological bechina equation. Without explicit 'X הוא בחינת Y' language, this is not a bechina cluster — it is a description of the practice itself. No new package.

2. MAKING TORAH INTO PRAYER / DIVINE DELIGHT cluster: The Rebbe says making Torah into prayer produces 'שַׁעֲשׁוּעִים גְּדוֹלִים מְאֹד לְמַעְלָה' (great divine delights above). The relationship is explicitly causal: 'מִזֶּה נַעֲשֶׂה שַׁעֲשׁוּעִים' — 'from this it BECOMES divine delight.' This is a textbook eitza formulation (A produces B), not a bechina equivalence (A IS B). Already captured in the dataset as an eitza edge. No new package.

3. VERNACULAR LANGUAGE / HEART-DRAWING cluster: The Rebbe discusses how Yiddish (לשון אשכנז) draws the heart because the heart is accustomed to it. He is making a psychological observation about why vernacular is preferable — not equating vernacular with any spiritual concept by bechina. No new package.

4. READINESS WHEN WORDS FAIL cluster: The Rebbe discusses that even when one cannot speak, the very 'הֲכָנָה' (preparation/readiness) and longing to speak is itself good. This is a single isolated concept, not a multi-node bechina cluster. No new package.

SUMMARY: Torah LM2/25 is a hanhagah (practical guidance) text that the Rebbe himself describes as 'דֶּרֶךְ וְעֵצָה טוֹבָה' (a path and good advice). Its discourse mode is eitza throughout. No bechina-based packages can be legitimately proposed from this text. The teaching's structure is:
  [Hitbodedut] --eitza--> [Drawing close to God]
  [Making Torah into prayer] --eitza--> [Divine delight above]
These are two eitza chains, not bechina clusters.
